findings.where: shiploop_navigator.packet_head and render (the first lines of every print and of the packet file); shiploop_prompts RULES bullet "unpiped"; PrintedHeadTests
findings.observation: All 20 `complete` calls the model made (9 check-only, 11 real) ran as `... 2>&1 | head -N` (N 8 to 60, median 20; the 7 producer-packet prints used N = 50,30,30,40,14,30,25), so it saw 12% to 43% of each producer packet (3.4 to 7.4 KB of 17 to 29 KB) and opened the packet file in 3 of 8 producer stages (one Read of 29,175 chars, two label greps). The only file pointer ("Full packet: ... Read the full packet before acting") is printed line 49 of the 1.3.0 step-plan head and reached the model in 3 of 8 prints, followed once; RULES "unpiped" was read once (step-plan) and the next call piped. Applying the 7 cut lengths to main's offline heads (node-fix-bug, inline, 49 cells, projection): callback and Goal visible 100%, status 76%, result template 24%, duties 29%, loop Start 0%, RULES 0%, file pointer 0%.
findings.proposal: Move the "Full packet:" line and "Read it with a file-reading tool, not by printing it to the shell" up into one pointer paragraph on line 2 of every print (packet_head and the whole-print path) and of the packet file; keep the sentence "References it names are for lookup: open only the section a step needs, never a whole reference file, and do not re-read the ShipLoop skill card" where it is (SKILL.md and references/* were read 0 times). Offsets: the separate Recovery line (about 330 chars with its command) becomes the last clause below, and the standalone "Never end the turn..." line duplicates a RULES bullet. Text: "Full packet: <RUN abs>/packets/<action>.md. Open it with the file tool before acting: the steps (Current stage guidance:), result template, loop command (Exit when ALL), RULES and original request are in it, and a print cut by | head leaves them out. Run every ShipLoop command exactly as printed, with no pipe, 2>&1 or variable, so the status display sees it. After lost context: python3 <CLI> next --run-dir=<RUN>". Test: for every stage x route the first 4 printed lines hold the packet path and the callback, and `head -12` of the print contains the Goal.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: no domain word; a host that never cuts output loses nothing.
findings.risk: A model that now opens the whole file adds up to the file size to its ingest (step-plan: 12,417 head + 29,175 file); the S-6 battery must show duties-read up and refusals not up before any saving is credited. The header line must stay line 1 (the status hook's HEADER test).
findings.plan_ref: 3.3 and 5.5 (first-lines text has no packet-file or as-printed line), 1.2, 3.2(d); the plan never records that the model cuts its own output (LEARNINGS 2026-10-16 calls it interim)
findings.est_effect: File pointer visible in 0 of 49 projected cuts today, in all 49 after; head size about -100 chars; no duty-read gain is claimed until measured.

findings.where: test/shiploop_e2e/run.py SEED_SCRIPT (nav.apply + nav.save) versus shiploop_lint.on_transition -> capture_base; shiploop_item_scope.commit_item
findings.observation: The seeded slice never captured W1's item base, so four gates the page describes did not run: tests/*-base1.md and *-mutation1.md say "skipped: no item base was recorded", lint/*-inventory.md is "unavailable", lint ran on the "fallback base ... report-only", and git log holds 2 commits (no "feat: W1"). Yet the carry-forward packet lists "W1 verify item commit: the commit whose subject starts feat: W1" and the system-test-author status prints "W1 is committed" (the model's own summary). The page's open item "the mutation check found no mutants ... Math.floor to Math.ceil" is a different cause in this run: the gate was skipped. Cause: SEED_SCRIPT advances the run without the transition that calls capture_base when an item is first entered.
findings.proposal: In SEED_SCRIPT, after the last synthetic stage, write the dict `shiploop_lint.capture_base(run_dir, Path(state["repo"]), item["id"])` returns (same as on_transition); make the slice fail or warn when any tests/*-base1.md or *-mutation1.md of the run says "skipped" for "no item base"; and have `commit_item` print "ShipLoop could not read the item's changes; nothing was committed." when `changed_paths` is None, instead of returning silently.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: harness and a generic message.
findings.risk: The base run will start refusing a new test ID that passes on base, so refusal counts and time rise; compare against a new control, not the old one.
findings.plan_ref: none (1.1 baseline rows inherit this gap)
findings.est_effect: A slice PASS then covers base run, mutation, change inventory and item commit; every earlier node-fix-bug slice baseline is a run without them.

findings.observation: Only the first command (`next`) was literal. None of the 20 `complete` commands was: 19 used `--run-dir=$R` (17 also `python3 $SC`), 1 a relative `--run-dir=run`, all 20 ended `2>&1 | head -N`; every loop call after the first used `$P`/`$R` (assignments in 41 calls: R= 25, P= 18, A= 18, SC= 17); 91 typings of the 118-char output prefix are 27% of the 39,513 chars the model typed into tool calls. I ran `_verb` on main: it returns None for `... 2>&1`, for `| head` and for `python3 $SC complete`, and a verb for the plain literal command; `COMMAND_RUN_DIR` misses `$SC` (the session stayed bound from the first `next`). So the status display fired once in 21 ShipLoop commands (events.jsonl: one "PostToolUse:Bash says") and metrics.narrative is emitted 3, shown 0. The RULES bullet "unpiped" already exists and was ignored 20 of 20.
findings.proposal: Do not rely on text. Make the display hook tolerate what the model actually types: in `_verb` (a) accept a trailing `2>&1`, (b) accept a trailing `| head -N`, `| tail -N` or `| cat`, (c) expand same-command `NAME=value` assignments into later `$NAME` tokens before the basename test; the same in `COMMAND_RUN_DIR`. Test: the 21 recorded command shapes of this run as fixture strings map to the expected verb. Re-count literal commands after X-1; keep the plan's 3.2(d) bullet only as a measured line.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: parses command text, no host or domain assumption.
findings.risk: Parsing model-written shell inside one command string only (no execution); a mis-parse shows no display, which is today's behaviour. A `| head` cut can still remove the status block; X-4 puts it at line 9 to 13.
findings.plan_ref: 3.2(d) and principles 2 and 5: "hooks must see every command". The aim stands; the mechanism fails, because text did not keep commands literal in 0 of 20 calls, and the plan's own rejected-launcher reasoning assumes the model types what is printed.
findings.est_effect: Display 1 of 21 commands today; every shape in this run becomes visible where the status block survives the cut.

findings.where: shiploop_expectations._TEST_CASE_SHAPE and the "Fix case requirements" refusal; the test-spec template
findings.observation: The 3 refusals are all `--check-only`, all test-spec, none on a real complete (11 of 11 accepted first time; 9 check-only runs caught everything). R1: `test_cases[0] needs exactly id, criterion, requirement, oracle, red, green` (the row omitted requirement although the template and duty 2 name it). R2: the same refusal replayed because BSD `sed -i` failed and Edit refused an unread file (3 wasted calls, host tooling). R3: "TC-1 names R-3" has no entry in HOME/spec.md: the model copied R-3 from `_TEST_CASE_SHAPE` (`"requirement": "R-3"`) while the packet template printed R-1; the seed wrote no spec, so the model created docs/shiploop/spec.md with an invented R-3 and ShipLoop committed it (commit 2d09996).
findings.proposal: Replace the literal in `_TEST_CASE_SHAPE` with `R-<n>`; in the "Fix case requirements" refusal print the ids the spec holds ("HOME/spec.md has R-1, R-2") or, when it holds none, "HOME/spec.md has no R-<n> entry: report revise naming the missing requirement". Print a test_cases skeleton in the test-spec template: one row per focused-command id, `criterion` from that command's `criteria`, `requirement` from the criterion text when it names an R-<n>; the model fills oracle, red and green.
findings.risk: The skeleton must stay overridable and print nothing it cannot derive.
findings.plan_ref: 7.1(c) derived bookkeeping and 8.1 defects; the plan does not list a test_cases skeleton or the example-id mismatch
findings.est_effect: R1 and R3 avoided: 4 of the stage's 8 calls (R2's two tooling calls, the retry and the spec write); the invented-requirement path closes.

works_well: Literal callback plus `complete --check-only`: 9 check-only runs caught all 3 refusals; 11 of 11 real completes were accepted first time; the refusal text carried the exact shape (R1) and the cause plus path (R3) and the model fixed it in the next edit.

Script-owned navigation: each `complete` printed the next callback and status; `next` was needed once (the seed prompt's command), no stage was mis-ordered, 11 actions completed in 41 calls, validate-existing recorded by script with 0 turns.

Section labels are used as anchors: "Current stage guidance", "Argument:" and "Exit when" were grepped for 2.8 and 5.5 KB slices instead of whole 17 to 27 KB files (2 of 2 after step-plan); the ADAPTER section named in the packet was read as 2,550 chars, not 24 KB. Keep the labels stable.

A Goal line that names the result fields (implement: "exit codes go to RUN/notes/<action>.md, uncovered behaviour to `not_covered`") plus Checked-by in the first 5 lines was enough for 5 of 5 later stages (implement to carry-forward) to pass their gates without the model reading their duties, on a trivial item.
Improve packets (2 to 3 KB, two literal steps, printed whole) were followed exactly in 4 of 4; Claude's 2 KB preview of an over-limit `cat` kept the 42 KB handoff out of the context.
The harness already records the evidence this review needed (events.jsonl usage and timestamps, metrics.json stages, shiploop_failures, packets.read, tests/*.md skipped, HEAD_END on heads).
not_measured: Recovery after a clear or compaction: none occurred (context grew monotonically, no fresh start); the first-line pointer, `next` and a start-here card are not tested by this run.

The true printed head size on Claude: the 1.3.0 build prints no HEAD_END and the model cut every reply; the 1.5.0 heads were measured only by offline render with a short run dir (about 70 chars), not live.
Whether unseen duties lowered quality: only PASS verdicts on a one-line fix; no seeded defect, no blind rubric.
The basis of the page's "before" column and the builder script (not in the repo); inferred from today's raw sizes.
Whether a normal plugin install registers the until-loop skill (the harness loads one --plugin-dir).
A/A spread for time, turns and tokens; dollar cost; thinking tokens per stage; per-event latency split between model and tools.
Other hosts: whether Grok or Codex cut output the same way on 1.5.0 (LEARNINGS says Claude cuts in most calls and varies between runs).
